title: History's Greatest Traitors
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explore the history of "traitors" and the meaning of the word "trader" (Benedict Arnold, Brutus and Cassius, Judas, Jesse James's killer Robert Ford, Mata Hari, Tokyo Rose, and Vidkun Quisling). The episode opens with a Brady Bunch-inspired bit about Peter Brady being called "Benedict Donald," then covers each figure's background, betrayal, and fate, noting where historical claims are disputed (Mata Hari was likely not a spy; Judas's Gospel reinterpretation). It closes with a listener letter from Jill Overturf about her father's vascular dementia and Alzheimer's, which prompted thanks for the episode on Capgras syndrome.

entities.name: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford

segments.title: Brady Bunch 'Benedict Donald' bit and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh recounts a Brady Bunch episode in which Peter Brady is cast as Benedict Arnold and classmates call him a traitor. The hosts introduce the episode's topic of traders and note that 'Benedict Donald' is still used as an insult.

segments.title: Benedict Arnold
segments.summary: Arnold's early life: family wealth lost through his father's bad dealings, schooling trouble, apothecary work, and merchant success. He joined the Sons of Liberty, had a military career with support from Washington and Jefferson, and felt slighted. He was put in charge of West Point and sold war secrets to the British for about 10,000 pounds. After the plot was intercepted he was convicted of treason, joined the British Army, and was later disappointed in England and Canada. His name was erased from a West Point plaque.

segments.title: Brutus and Cassius and the assassination of Caesar
segments.summary: Cassius and Brutus, who had fought against Caesar and were pardoned, took part in the assassination of Julius Caesar on the Ides of March in 44 BC. Cassius was motivated by envy and used the idea of Rome becoming a dictatorship to recruit Brutus. Caesar was stabbed about 23 times, and reportedly said 'et tu, Brute.' The hosts also discuss who struck first and the Dante Inferno depiction.

segments.title: Judas Iscariot and the Gospel of Judas
segments.summary: Judas's betrayal of Jesus with a kiss for thirty pieces of silver, his remorse, suicide, and the potter's field. The hosts discuss the Gospel of Judas, a second-century Coptic text that portrays Judas as following Jesus's wishes, and scholarly debate over its translation, including April DeConick's criticism.

segments.title: Jesse James and Robert Ford
segments.summary: Jesse James, leader of the James Gang, was shot in the back of the head in 1882 by Robert Ford, who had joined the gang and collected a bounty from the Governor of Missouri. Ford and his brother were pardoned in a single day, became social outcasts, and Ford was later killed by Edward O'Kelly in a bar. The hosts mention the film about the killing.
